summary: Oxygen-free and low resistivity nickel (Ni) thin films are successfully prepared by plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition (ALD) using nickelocene (NiCp2) as a metal precursor and ammonia (NH3) as a reactant. The films exhibit excellent conformality on Si nano-pillars and show a significant reduction in resistivity after post-annealing at 400 oC in forming gas (N2/4%-H2).
evidence: Oxygen-free and low resistivity nickel (Ni) thin films are successfully prepared by plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition (ALD) using nickelocene (NiCp2) as a metal precursor and ammonia (NH3) as a reactant. The results indicate that the as-deposited films are a Ni-dominated material with small quantities of C and N, containing Ni−Ni, Ni−C, Ni−N, C−N and C−C bonds. Moreover, the films also exhibit excellent conformality on Si nano-pillars with an aspect ratio of ~13. After being annealed at 400 oC in forming gas (N2/4%-H2), the resistivity is reduced significantly down to 11.8 μΩ·cm, and the work function increases up to 4.136 eV.
